description: The evolution policy (the Successor Tech Lead Directive §13): how the repository observes, researches, authorizes and implements change — reusing Zeck's EXISTING authorities (identity/policy/capabilities/budget/execution/verification/evidence/learning). There is NO independent 'evolution authority': the evolution program is a GOVERNANCE LOOP over the same seams, the same work-order discipline and the same evidence rules as every other program.
loop: OBSERVE — the nightly scan + event triggers collect the observable facts (dependency releases, route/manifest drift, journey-coverage state, the gap ledger)
DETECT — a delta becomes a CANDIDATE change only when it maps to a gap-ledger entry or a journey-coverage regression (no speculative rewrites)
RESEARCH — the candidate's upstream truth is collected (release notes, docs, the provider's own artifacts) and recorded in the run log; never from memory (the zero-drift rule)
COMPARE — the candidate is mapped against the solution catalog + the conformance contracts (is an existing solution's substitution the answer, or a new adapter?)
MAP — the blast radius is computed: which ports, adapters, manifests, tests, docs and journeys the change touches (the conflict-partition discipline)
AUTHORIZE — a governed work order is issued (or an existing one amended); the never-authorized list below is absolute
IMPLEMENT — the worker rules: one branch, one work order, no self-merge, no spec/development-state edits, battery-verified
VERIFY — the Lead's review + independent battery (the merge gate)
CANARY — the change lands on the preview plane first (the §13.6 chain), never straight to a wider surface
MEASURE — the journey coverage + public-smoke re-run at the exact attested revision; regressions are findings
PROMOTE / ROLLBACK — per the promotion policy (promotion-policy.json)
LEARN — the run record + the gap ledger + the solution catalog are updated with the outcome

cadence.nightlyScan: dependency + manifest + route drift (the OBSERVE step's routine sweep)
cadence.eventTriggered: a journey-coverage regression, a public-smoke failure, an upstream breaking release, or an operator notice
cadence.weeklyDeepDive: one architectural concern per week examined at depth (rotating through the gap ledger)

triggerAuthority: external cron/schedules are TRIGGERS only — the scheduler is never the authority; authorization is always the governed work order

autonomyLevels.0: manual — every change is a human/operator-approved work order
autonomyLevels.1: observed — the program collects facts and files findings, changes nothing
autonomyLevels.2: drafted — the program may prepare research + comparison records for a human decision
autonomyLevels.3: gated — the program may prepare a work-order DRAFT for the Lead's authorization
autonomyLevels.4: pre-authorized low-risk — adapter-internal changes (dependency pins within a semver-compatible range, conformance-suite extensions) may be auto-promoted through the canary + measure gates, with rollback armed
autonomyLevels.5: delegated — broader autonomy, only ever granted by an explicit operator-recorded decision

neverAutomaticallyPromoted: the authority chain (identity, policy, capabilities, budget, execution, verification)
any change that weakens verification or evidence rules
any change that alters what counts as execution success
evidenceRules: the maturity model's evidence chain governs every claim: neutral contract → fake conformance → local integration → real credentialed execution → repeatable journey → failure drill → alternate solution → production observation; an unavailable external is recorded NOT RUN, never a PASS by simulation
